items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: to the clarinets like Lorenzo T.O. Jr.

ctx.x: You said you were in the studio, you told him. Right.

You were there, of course. Well, it's a banjo, uh, like, and, of course, you had another great one, but I don't think he was quite as great as Caffer. It was John, John Morello. Well, he was, he was tremendous. Then, all right, then you go down into, uh, to the clarinets like Lorenzo T.O. Jr. Uh, and the old man, uh, we called him Papai. Uh, huh. That taught all of us how he's a symphony man. Uh, huh. Those guys read music just like the newspaper. I imagine that. I was talking to my professors' daughters last…

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: And there's now, there's still a Louis Teo living who was a brother of young Lorenzo, the very fine clarinetist.

ctx.x: Well, that's the old man. Papa. That's what we call him.
And there's now, there's still a Louis Teo living who was a brother of young Lorenzo, the very fine clarinetist.

So one brother is still living there. He's still living, but I don't remember him. But the one that finished, well, anyhow, Bonnie went to, he says, well, come on, Papa, I'll take you over. So I went over to one day with him. And Bonnie took his lessons first. Then after he went through his, he was already playing the clarinet, but I hadn't even decided on the horn yet.
